newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent closes mixed as March expires quietly.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent closes mixed as March expires quietly.

text.p: IPE Brent crude closed mixed as the expiring prompt March contract shed three cents and April firmed in a wave of market-on-close buying, brokers said.
Mar Brent expired at $20.49 a barrel, right in the middle of the day's 40-cent range, while April gained 11 cents to $20.35.
"There was some good buying at the close all round the ring which caught a few people by surprise but otherwise the expiry was fairly uneventful," said a broker.
After dipping as low as $19.96, April steadied to close above the psychologically important $20.00, helped by technical factors and a recovery in U.S. heating oil prices.
Prompt Brent futures last traded below $20.00 on August 28.
"There was good support later in the session as (NYMEX) heating oil bounced off the low of 59.45 (cents a gallon) but the fundamental outlook is still not great," said a broker.
With demand for heating oil waning as winter retreats and the spring gasoline season still some way off, brokers expect Brent to suffer from surging crude supply.
Wednesday's news that Iraq may have to sell crude oil on the spot market to make up for a shortfall in revenue from the U.N. oil-for-food programme was adding to the pressure.
"That can't be good for the market," said a trader.
Earlier, March IPE gas oil closed $4.50 a tonne weaker after finding comfortable support at $178.50 and trading in a well-defined range around $180 a tonne, brokers said.
March closed at $180.25 a tonne after the early weak performance on U.S. heating oil dislodged the contract from the $181-$182 range.
"Gas oil just consolidated at a lower level in reasonable volume, nothing special. Brent saw the real action today," a trader said.
